textbookText: Let’s discuss the following questions: i. What are the stimuli? ii. Do all plants and animals respond to stimuli? The response of animals to stimuli is more remarkable? Why? iii. Do you know that a baby crocodile starts to swim after being hatched? Why? iv. Have you heard the loud sound of frogs with inflated sacs in their throat on rainy days? What might be the reason behind it?

The activity of all the living beings i.e. from microscopic to higher organism is influenced by environmental factors. Any external environmental factors, such as heat, cold, touch, pain, chemical, light, sound etc. are called stimuli. In unicellular organisms, individual cell itself responds to stimuli. For instance: Euglena moves towards glucose solution. Higher animals have well developed nervous system and hence degree of sensitivity is remarkable in them. However, some plant like Touch Me Not (Mimosa pudica) also responds to touch by immediate overlapping of leaves. Similarly, directional growth of plant parts in response to stimuli like sunlight, chemical, earth etc. is called tropism. When mosquito repellent is burnt inside the room, mosquitos fly away. In all of the above cases, reactions shown by the organisms against stimuli are called responses.

Animals behaviour is the outwardly expressed course of action produced in organism in response to stimulus from a given situation. Behaviour helps animal for adaptation in the particular environment. Ethology is the study of animal behaviour. Ethology may also be defined as the study of behaviour of animals in their normal environment including both external and internal processes by which they respond to change in environment. Khorad Lorenz is the father of ethology.
Animal behaviour may be broadly classified as: 1. Innate or inborn or stereotyped behaviour:

Behaviours which are genetically controlled and inherent, without patent learning during life time are called innate behaviour. This kind of behaviour is essentially the outcome of inherited properties of nervous system of the organism. Example: Fish, tortoise etc. starts swimming just after emerging from the egg. Young spider spins web without learning from parents, larva of silkworm forms cocoon etc.
Reflexes, taxis, migration, courtship, leadership, dominance, kinesis etc. are the various types of innate behaviour.

2. Acquired or learnt behaviour: All those behaviours which an animal learns during its life time through experience and practice are known as learnt behaviour. This type of behaviour is not inherited from parents to progeny. Examples: singing, dancing, painting, learning languages etc. 9.2.2 REFLEX ACTION

Questions to think? What is the reason for watering your mouth when you see or get smell of delicious food? In higher animals, many responses are involuntary and instantaneous. These responses occur without prior thinking. Example: watering of mouth occur at the sight or smell of delicious food, immediate withdrawal of hand or leg when stepped on sharp objects, blinking of eye when some object is about to fall on eyes, taking immediate support by an individual while S/he is about to fall down from chair, coughing triggered by allergens etc. these all action are reflex action. Thus reflex action is the involuntary or instant and automated response of an animal towards stimuli. Reflex action is of following types: a. Spinal reflexes: Reflex actions which involve spinal cord and nerves. Example: knee jerking, withdrawing hand from fire etc. b. Cerebral reflexes: Reflex actions which involve brain and nerves. Example: Eye blinking, sneezing, watering of mouth etc. c. Both cerebral and spinal reflexes: Reflex actions which involve both brain and spinal cord along with nerves. Example: Hunger, coughing, hiccupping etc.
